solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Twisted elastic around skirt top for princess

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap round the single letter taken from skirt
twisted out of shape, so the letters of elastic are rearranged
the top of skirt is its first letter, as a down-the-page reading would put it

explanation.surface: A princess fiddling with a waistband that has come loose at the top of her skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' rearranges ELASTIC to ALCETIS, and 'around' puts the S from 'skirt top' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Alcestis was a princess, daughter of King Pelias, who died in place of her husband Admetus.

clue.text: Off course, Vauxhall car by yard

parts.note: the Astra is a long-running Vauxhall model

explanation.surface: A driver in a Vauxhall has wandered off course near a yard.
explanation.walkthrough: Vauxhall is a British car maker; the Astra is one of its family hatchbacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone astray has wandered from its proper route, so it is off course.

clue.text: Councillor from the city — chap at nursery

parts.note: EC, the postcode district, stands for the City of London
a chap is a male, he

explanation.surface: A local councillor from town visits a man at a children's nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postal district of the City of London, the financial square mile.
explanation.definitionFit: A crèche is a day nursery where small children are looked after while parents work.

clue.text: Military cap has to be waved at kick-off

indicators.note: something waved about is shaken up, so the letters of has are rearranged

parts.note: KO is the usual abbreviation for kick-off on football fixture lists

explanation.surface: A soldier's cap is waved in the air when the match begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a tall cylindrical peaked hat with a plume, worn by soldiers in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: European in the same place with monarch and Scot

parts.note: IB, short for Latin ibidem, means in the same place in footnotes
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch
Ian is the Scottish form of John, a typical Scots name

explanation.surface: A European finds himself alongside a king and a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iberian comes from the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal, so is a European.

clue.text: Alien visitor embraced by this nereid

indicators.note: embraced by says the alien sits within the following word

parts.note: taken as written
ET is the film's extra-terrestrial visitor

explanation.surface: A sea nymph hugs a visitor from outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: The nereids were the fifty sea-nymph daughters of Nereus; Thetis, mother of Achilles, is the best known.

clue.text: Awkward matter seeing sexy Charlotte?

parts.note: sexy means hot
Charlotte is a variety of salad potato, so a potato by example, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A tricky situation arises from seeing an attractive woman named Charlotte.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlotte' looks like a woman's name; it is a popular variety of potato.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an idiom for a controversial issue that nobody wants to handle.

clue.text: Suite, play and film

definitions.meaning: Respighi's orchestral suite Gli Uccelli bears this title in English
Aristophanes wrote a comedy of this name about a city in the clouds
Hitchcock's 1963 thriller of feathered attackers has this title

explanation.surface: A list of artistic works: a musical suite, a stage play and a film.
explanation.definitionFit: Respighi's suite, Aristophanes' comedy and Hitchcock's thriller all share this one title.

clue.text: Wrenches for bridges?

definitions.meaning: tools for turning nuts and bolts
bridges are things that span a gap

explanation.surface: Asks whether wrenches might be used for building bridges.
explanation.definitionFit: British English calls wrenches spanners, and a bridge spans a river, so it is jokily a spanner too.

clue.text: Goddesses chew this when arguing two points

parts.note: to chew the fat is to chat or grumble at length, so that is what one chews
E and S, east and south, are two compass points

explanation.surface: Goddesses chew something while they bicker over a couple of points.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'chew the fat' means to talk or grumble at length, supplying the first six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fates were the three Greek goddesses who spun, measured and cut the thread of life.

clue.text: Goddess gets consistently good exam grades

parts.note: an A grade, then another A: a top grade followed by the same again
then is the word linking one A to the next
the second A grade, repeating the first

explanation.surface: A goddess with a run of excellent exam results.
explanation.walkthrough: Consistently good grades are 'A, then A', read straight off as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena was the Greek goddess of wisdom, fittingly for someone with top marks.

clue.text: Peddle drugs from the inside, allegedly

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows, spanning the comma

parts.note: selling drugs is ..., and an inside ... is one done by someone on the inside, as rumour has it

explanation.surface: Someone allegedly sells drugs from inside a prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' looks like part of the indicator, but its last two letters start the answer, which runs on into 'allegedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal is the slang verb for selling illegal drugs, as a dealer does.

clue.text: Badly atrophied goddess

indicators.note: badly treated, so the letters of the next word are disordered

explanation.surface: A goddess whose muscles have wasted away.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite was the Greek goddess of love and beauty, the counterpart of Venus.

clue.text: Hunter is opening batsman, apparently, run out, backing up

indicators.note: backing up means the assembled letters run backwards

parts.note: the opener is number one, No 1, which looks like NOI
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for out

explanation.surface: A cricket report: the opening batsman has been run out while backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' says No 1 is read as letters, NO plus I. In cricket, backing up is the non-striker leaving the crease early, often how a run-out happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion is the giant hunter of Greek myth, placed among the stars as a constellation.

clue.text: Job centre row in Valhalla

indicators.note: the centre of a three-letter word is its middle letter

parts.note: a row is a din, a loud noise

explanation.surface: A dispute at the job centre, set in the hall of the Norse gods.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the setting: Odin presides over Valhalla.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin, the chief Norse god, rules Valhalla, the hall where slain warriors feast.

clue.text: Newspaper department popular on Sundays, snapping Queen in leathers

indicators.note: to snap is to catch up in the jaws, so the newspaper department takes the queen inside

parts.note: a desk is a section of a newspaper office, such as the news desk
ER, Elizabeth Regina
in means popular, fashionable
S is the abbreviation for Sunday

explanation.surface: A popular Sunday supplement desk photographs the Queen in leather clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Deerskins are hides of deer made into leather, so leathers made from that animal.

clue.text: Swimmer showing how to spell "ogle" in two halves

indicators.note: showing how to spell the synonym for ogle lays out its two halves with the joining word between them

parts.note: to ogle is to leer
a word written in two halves is its first half 'and' its second half, so the joining word is and

explanation.surface: A swimmer shows how a word should be spelt in two halves.
explanation.walkthrough: Ogle means leer; spelt in two halves it is the first half 'and' the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to meet his lover Hero, and drowned in a storm.

clue.text: Class base supporting Mr Low turning up

parts.note: supporting means for, in favour of
taken as the abbreviation for mister

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up reads the word from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: A class backs a man called Mr Low who has just arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' is the cow's call, not a surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A form room is a school class's home room, the base where a form registers.

clue.text: PM, done in, shattered, now receptive to new ideas

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for the noun state of being open-minded

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: An exhausted Prime Minister is now willing to consider fresh ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Done in' and 'shattered' both look like tiredness; the second is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Having an open mind means being willing to consider fresh opinions rather than prejudging.

clue.text: Sup with Hero disguised as musician

indicators.note: disguised means altered in appearance, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Having supper with a hero who is in disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpheus was the legendary Thracian lyre player whose music charmed beasts and the underworld.

clue.text: Location of 5 requiring backing somewhat

indicators.note: requiring backing says the letters are read in reverse
somewhat means only part of the word given by the cross-reference

parts.note: 5 refers to the answer at 5 across, the nereid

explanation.surface: Asks where clue 5 is located, needing some support.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a place or position where something is found.

clue.text: Half-complete god

indicators.note: half signals that only the first half of the synonym is used

parts.note: complete, as in a total job, means thorough

explanation.surface: A god who is only partly finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Thor is the hammer-wielding Norse god of thunder.

clue.text: Literary heroine having time for piece of mosaic work

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Hardy's heroine
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A literary heroine has time to work on a mosaic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is a small square tile of stone or glass used to make a mosaic.

clue.text: Clash having released daughter's dog

indicators.note: having released means letting a letter go free, so it is dropped

parts.note: to clash is to collide
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: After a quarrel, a daughter's dog is set free.
explanation.definitionFit: The collie is a Scottish sheepdog breed, such as the Border collie.

clue.text: Rent payer from the French diocese

parts.note: les is the plural form of the in French
a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A tenant who pays rent to a French diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee holds property under a lease and pays the landlord rent for it.

clue.text: Juniors having no right to be king

indicators.note: having no says the letter for right is left out

parts.note: juniors are minors, people under age

explanation.surface: Young people with no right to rule as king.
explanation.definitionFit: Minos was the legendary king of Crete whose labyrinth housed the Minotaur.

clue.text: It's me on the blower in fury

parts.note: an archaic way to say it's me is 'tis I
the blower is British slang for the telephone

explanation.surface: An angry caller announces herself down the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fury' looks like rage; it means one of the Furies, the avenging spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Tisiphone was one of the three Furies, the Erinyes, who avenged murder.

clue.text: Blended a type of whisky?

indicators.note: blended means mixed together, so the letters are rearranged, apt for whisky

explanation.surface: Asks about a blended kind of whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue serves as definition: a mix of 'a type' describes a whisky's character.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaty describes the smoky flavour of whiskies made with malt dried over peat fires.

clue.text: God's very large flag

parts.note: OS is short for outsize, very large
the yellow flag is a type of iris

explanation.surface: A god owns a huge banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' is not a banner here; it is the iris plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was the Egyptian god of the dead and the afterlife.

clue.text: Champion removed thong from broken clothes hanger

indicators.note: removed says the letters of thong are taken away
broken means the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A champion takes a thong off a broken clothes hanger.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T, H, O, N and G from CLOTHES HANGER and rearrange the remaining CLESHAER.
explanation.definitionFit: Heracles, Hercules to the Romans, was the great hero and strongman of Greek myth.

clue.text: Gorgon at sea across the pond

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
across the pond, the Atlantic, means America, the USA

explanation.surface: A monster is at sea, crossing the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Medusa was the snake-haired Gorgon whose gaze turned onlookers to stone.

clue.text: Beautiful youth, awfully mean and edgy

indicators.note: awfully means badly done, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A handsome young man is described as nasty and tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganymede was the beautiful Trojan boy carried off by Zeus to be cupbearer of the gods.
